title: Finite group quotients preserve relative projectivity
statement: Let $B$ be a Noetherian scheme quasi-projective over an affine Noetherian scheme, and let $V\to B$ be quasi-projective of finite type. Quasi-projective means admitting a locally closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over the base. Let a finite group $H$ act on $V$ over $B$. Then there exists a categorical geometric quotient $q:V\to Q=V/H$ in schemes. The morphism $q$ is finite and surjective, its geometric fibres are the orbits, $\mathcal O_Q=(q_*\mathcal O_V)^H$, and $Q\to B$ is quasi-projective of finite type. If $V\to B$ is projective, then $Q\to B$ is projective in the finite-projective-space convention [def-kun-projective]. If $V$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], then $Q$ is integral. Restricting to any $H$-invariant open of $V$ gives its quotient as the corresponding open of $Q$. Finite morphisms and finite type are as in [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Categorical means that every $H$-invariant morphism from $V$ to a scheme factors uniquely through $q$.

source.place: WANTED locally. Rydh, Existence and properties of geometric quotients, arXiv:0708.3333v2, Theorem 4.4, Proposition 4.7, Remark 4.9, pp.20--23 (read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/0708.3333). The ample-base hypothesis ensures that projectivity also has the finite-projective-space meaning.

proof.text: Finite type over the Noetherian B makes V locally Noetherian, and quasi-compactness makes it Noetherian. Apply the proved absolute-ampleness theorem for the quasi-projective tower. Its Segre composition is explicitly proved and uses no relative-twist prerequisite.

source.place: Original Step 1, with the shorter proved Segre argument

proof.text: Apply the invariant-affine quotient construction to the ample source, obtaining Q,r,q, its admissible finite quotient structure, surjectivity, actual geometric-fibre transitivity, the categorical property, local finite type over B and arbitrary invariant-open restrictions.

The underlying topology of V is Noetherian. Its continuous surjective image Q is Noetherian (pull back any open cover and a finite subcover descends by surjectivity). Every subset of Q is compact, so r is quasi-compact. Apply ampleness on an existing admissible quotient to obtain M on Q.

The immersion for b gives b locally of finite type. Apply the ample immersion theorem to Q→B→S≅Spec Γ(S,⊤); its current Lean conclusion is already an immersion into the canonical finite projective space, not an unrelated relative Proj. ProjectiveSpace.liftBaseChange along B→Spec Γ(S,⊤) gives an immersion over B, with exactly the same finite coordinate type.

source.place: Original Step 10, using the source-library lift API

proof.text: If p is H-projective, its canonical proved source instance makes it proper. UniversallyClosed.of_comp_surjective descends universal closedness through q. Quasi-projectivity makes r separated, and local finite type then makes it proper. The chosen immersion i:Q→P^n_B is proper by IsProper.of_comp, since its structural composite is r and projective space is separated. The closed-image criterion makes i a closed immersion and gives IsHProjective r.

source.place: Original Step 11, with the existing Mathlib universal-closedness cancellation

proof.text: If V is integral, every section ring of V is reduced. The sectionwise injection in the admissible quotient predicate makes each section ring of Q reduced. The continuous surjective image of the irreducible V is irreducible, including nonemptiness. The reduced/irreducible characterization gives IsIntegral Q. Assemble these proved consequences with the construction output; no new assumption or weaker conclusion is used.
